content: 1. Tecovirimat is a weak inducer of CYP3A4 enzymes. It can reduce the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised when co-administering these drugs. Additionally, sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness during co-administration. 2. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases temsirolimus levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. After discontinuing cobicistat, a one-week washout period is advised before increasing the temsirolimus dose to its original level. 3. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir also increases terbinafine levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir also increases theophylline levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of thioridazine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 may be necessary during co-administration. 8. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases tiagabine levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of timolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 10. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases tinidazole levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both darunavir and tipranavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Its active metabolite, MMAE, is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to unconjugated MMAE, raising the risk of adverse effects. Similarly, darunavir also increases tisotumab vedotin levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 14. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 may also inhibit toremifene metabolism. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tramadol by inhibiting both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. A reduced dose of tramadol may be necessary. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir also increases trazodone levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect. Monitor for antidepressant response. 18. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases triamcinolone levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir also increases trimipramine levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor its response during co-administration. 20. Ublituximab decreases the effects of darunavir due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir also increases umeclidinium/vilanterol levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 23. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases upadacitinib levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised when co-administering with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat increases valbenazine levels by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 25. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases vamorolone levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if the patient weighs more than 50 kg. 26. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases vardenafil levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases verapamil levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates, and co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 31. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases vinblastine levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure to vinblastine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. If the antiretroviral regimen must be withheld for a prolonged period, consider initiating a revised regimen that does not include a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases vincristine levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure to vincristine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 34. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with voriconazole is not recommended unless the benefit/risk assessment justifies its use. Similarly, cobicistat also increases voriconazole levels through the same mechanism. 35. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vortioxetine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 36. Darunavir may alter warfarin serum concentrations, either increasing or decreasing them. Similarly, cobicistat also affects warfarin levels. Monitor INR more frequently if co-administered with inhibitors of CYP3A4, CYP1A2, or CYP2C19, and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 37. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir also increases zanubrutinib levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. 39. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of zileuton by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary due to the potential for increased toxicity. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases zuranolone levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the zuranolone dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 41. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 43. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 44. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of aliskiren and alosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 45. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
